title: 3.1. Comparison Operators & Conditional Execution
summary: Learn equality (==), inequality (!=), and relational operators (<, <=, >, >=), and implement branching logic with if, if-else, and if-elif-else statements.
learningObjectives: Compare values using relational and equality operators.
Understand block indentation: Python's syntax structure replacing curly braces.
Construct multi-branch conditional trees using if, elif, and else.

sections.heading: 3.1.1 Comparison Operators & Truth Values
sections.content:
Computers make decisions by evaluating expressions that resolve to a boolean value: True or False.

Python provides six comparison operators:
• == : Equal to (DO NOT confuse with the assignment operator =)
• != : Not equal to
• > : Greater than
• >= : Greater than or equal to
• < : Less than
• <= : Less than or equal to

sections.heading: 3.1.2 The if-elif-else Conditional Structure
sections.content: In Python, code blocks are defined strictly by indentation (standard is 4 spaces). The if statement evaluates a boolean condition: if True, the indented block executes; otherwise, execution jumps to the next elif or else branch.

knowledgeChecks.prompt: Which operator tests for equality between two operands in Python?
knowledgeChecks.explanation: == is the equality comparison operator, whereas = is the assignment operator.

recap: Comparisons yield booleans; if-elif-else blocks control program execution paths through clean indentation.
